408.title: FR-5: Warping DOF is shared by all members at a node (full warping transmission); no per-member warping release

410.title: SH-6: Curved shell reports zero bending moments, and its stresses ignore thermal strain

411.title: SH-7: MITC9 on non-planar geometry does not reproduce rigid-body motion (advertised for curved shells)

412.title: SH-8: MITC9 tying points differ from Bucalem-Bathe; confirm the variant and cite it

413.title: SH-15: Shell docstrings disagree with the code (pressure load, EAS modes, lumped vs consistent mass)

415.title: SP-11: `ernst_tangent_modulus` is not the derivative of the chord-tension law

416.title: SP-12: Cable solver tension is too low in indeterminate systems (Ernst tangent used as a secant from the chord)

417.title: SP-14: Linear solver lets a cable carry compression with no diagnostic

418.title: SP-15: Curved-beam segment axes depend on plan orientation (Iy/Iz swap on near-vertical segments)

419.title: SP-17: 3D connector axes are discontinuous in direction and not user-orientable

420.title: SP-18: Fiber solvers return an empty reactions list

421.title: AC-12: p-y curves depart from the cited references (soft clay J term, sand A = 0.9, sand k table)

422.title: AC-13: "Stiff clay" p-y curve is discontinuous at y50 and is not Reese's stiff-clay curve

423.title: AC-16: t-z and q-z curves are missing the shaft perimeter / tip area (units kPa x m, not kN)

424.title: MD-6: Spectral element forces combined from per-mode absolute end values (CQC cross terms never negative)

425.title: MD-10: TimeHistoryInput.method is ignored; the scheme follows `alpha` alone

426.title: NL-3: 3D co-rotational uses additive rotation vectors: error for large non-coaxial rotations

427.title: NL-4: Material-nonlinear solver reports elastic member forces K_el u (100x off after yield)

428.title: NL-5: Material-nonlinear solver is a whole-member secant (EI -> alpha EI), not plasticity

429.title: NL-6: 3D material-nonlinear yield surface is unconservative compared with 2D

431.title: NL-10: Notional loads ignore member (distributed/point) gravity loads

433.title: NL-17: Fiber solver reports an unconverged iterate on failure (no load factor)

435.title: Flat 2D model solved in 3D: nodal moments and prescribed rotations act mirrored

442.title: Imperfection analysis can silently do nothing (3D gravity axis, member loads, residual stresses, plane model along Y)

444.title: Winkler member forces leave out the foundation reaction

safety_issues.title: Verification jobs that run on schedule and alert on failure
Discretization error estimates next to certified results
Units in the type system (Rust and TypeScript)
Missing design checks: RC biaxial/torsion/slenderness, CIRSOC 301 F.7-F.11, EC3 6.2.9.1 and more
Mechanism detection everywhere, with zero false positives on the corpus
Known solver gaps: unconverged nonlinear increments, co-rotational refusals, beam rotary inertia, and more
Trusted computing base of certificates: audited and enforced
Nonlinear and dynamic robustness: convergence criteria, step sensitivity, energy drift
Numerical stress tests: measure where accuracy degrades and refuse beyond it
Staging before production: deploy main to staging, promote tagged releases
Dependency upgrades through the same gates; numerics crates must stay bit-identical
Keep steel results labelled experimental until independent review of CIRSOC 301
Steel check inputs from the engine: Cb, J/Cw/Z, unbraced lengths, buckling, net area
Analysis results from the engine: remove TypeScript analysis duplicates
Footings and load generation (wind, snow, seismic, combinations) in Rust
No silent fallbacks: say so when the engine is unavailable
FR-5: Warping DOF is shared by all members at a node (full warping transmission); no per-member warping release
SP-14: Linear solver lets a cable carry compression with no diagnostic
SP-17: 3D connector axes are discontinuous in direction and not user-orientable
NL-3: 3D co-rotational uses additive rotation vectors: error for large non-coaxial rotations
NL-5: Material-nonlinear solver is a whole-member secant (EI -> alpha EI), not plasticity
NL-13: Contact solver reports converged after freezing a chattering gap at max_flips
NL-17: Fiber solver reports an unconverged iterate on failure (no load factor)
Safety advisories: notify users when a released version produced a wrong or unconservative result
Contain first, fix second: per-feature runtime switches (warn/refuse) for known dangerous results
3D buckling: compression gate uses end-force average, misses members compressed only between their ends
Existing (assembled-level) certificate certifies singular models: all-hinged 2D node with moment/rigid link; skew unstiffened rotation
2D constraint mapping assumes the X–Z plane; models cut along a Y–Z plane are mapped wrongly
Certified 3D buckling factor above its own certified upper bound (fuzz json_dynamics)
Test gap: 765 missed mutants in 49 functions survive in the plastic-collapse certificates
Test gap: 133 missed mutants in 12 functions survive in the plate element kernels (DKT, DKMT, CST)
Test gap: 119 missed mutants in 8 functions survive in the cable element (catenary)
Test gap: 214 missed mutants in 30 functions survive in the modal, spectral, harmonic and time-history certificates
Test gap: 160 missed mutants in 30 functions survive in the certificate's independent re-assembly
Test gap: 67 missed mutants in 23 functions survive in the design-check certificates
Test gap: 244 missed mutants in 50 functions survive in the static certificate support code
Test gap: 260 missed mutants in 21 functions survive in the frame, truss, curved-beam and fiber-beam kernels
2D plastic collapse factor changes with renumbering, member direction and units (up to 4.6x)
3D modal analysis returns modes that are not mass-orthogonal (one mode returned twice)
Linear time history violates reciprocity on some models (up to 33x between i<-j and j<-i)
Mechanism detection and accuracy change with units and orientation on near-singular models
Engine: MITC4 shells are badly stiff for in-plane bending on distorted meshes (MacNeal–Harder: −92% trapezoidal, −90% parallelogram)
Engine triage: MITC4 Scordelis–Lo roof plateaus 15% stiff; pinched cylinder error grows with refinement
Buckling: the dense reciprocal eigen-solve can report a factor slightly above the true one (0.05% in #741's case)
